title: Units Dimensional Analysis and Conversion Factors
description: Covers unit systems and dimensional analysis. Students learn to verify equation consistency and convert quantities across different measurement systems.

title: Correlations
description: Introduces empirical correlations used in chemical engineering. Students learn to apply and evaluate fitted equations that relate process variables from experimental data.

title: Iterative Solutions of Nonlinear Equations
description: Teaches numerical methods for solving nonlinear equations using Excel Solver. Students learn iterative techniques to find unknown variables in engineering calculations.

title: Manometry
description: Explains pressure measurement using manometers. Students learn to analyze U-tube and multi-fluid manometer configurations to determine pressure differences in fluid systems.

title: Material Balances
description: Covers steady-state material balances for chemical processes. Students learn to set up and solve mass balance equations for single and multi-unit systems.

title: Degrees of Freedom
description: Introduces degrees of freedom analysis for process systems. Students learn to determine whether a system is fully specified under-specified or over-specified before solving.

title: Recycle Mass Balances
description: Covers material balances for processes with recycle streams. Students learn to identify and solve balance equations around recycle loops in chemical processes.

title: Chemical Reactions
description: Explains stoichiometry and extent of reaction concepts. Students learn to write balanced equations and apply stoichiometric relationships in material balance problems.

title: Reactive Material Balances
description: Covers material balances for systems involving chemical reactions. Students learn to account for generation and consumption of species in reactive process balances.

title: Purge Stream in a System with Recycle
description: Explains material balances for processes with a purge stream and recycle. Students learn to determine purge flow rates to prevent inert accumulation in recycle systems.

title: Material Balances on Transient Processes
description: Covers unsteady-state material balances. Students learn to derive and solve differential equations describing time-varying mass accumulation in process systems.

title: Wet and Dry Basis
description: Explains wet basis and dry basis composition measurements. Students learn to convert between these bases for streams containing moisture commonly used in combustion and drying.

title: Combustion Reactions
description: Covers material balances for combustion reactions. Students learn to calculate flue gas compositions air-to-fuel ratios and percent excess air for combustion processes.

title: Ideal Gas Law
description: Introduces the ideal gas law and its applications. Students learn to use PV=nRT to relate pressure volume temperature and moles for ideal gas systems.

title: Equations of State
description: Covers cubic equations of state such as van der Waals Redlich-Kwong and Peng-Robinson. Students learn to calculate PVT properties of real gases and liquids.

title: Lever Rule
description: Explains the lever rule for determining phase compositions and fractions. Students learn to read two-phase regions on phase diagrams and calculate vapor and liquid fractions.

title: Single-Component Phase Equilibrium
description: Covers phase diagrams and equilibrium conditions for a single component. Students learn to identify phases and locate triple and critical points.

title: Clapeyron Clausius-Clapeyron and Antoine Equations
description: Explains the Clapeyron Clausius-Clapeyron and Antoine equations for vapor pressure. Students learn to estimate vapor pressure as a function of temperature.

title: Raoults Law and VLE
description: Covers vapor-liquid equilibrium using Raoults Law for ideal mixtures. Students learn to construct Pxy and Txy diagrams and solve bubble and dew point problems.

title: Solids in Solution and Colligative Properties
description: Explains behavior of solids dissolved in liquids and colligative properties. Students learn about boiling point elevation freezing point depression and osmotic pressure.

title: Ternary Phase Diagrams
description: Covers three-component phase diagrams for liquid-liquid and liquid-solid systems. Students learn to read ternary diagrams and determine compositions in multi-phase regions.

title: Water-Air VLE and Psychrometric Chart
description: Covers vapor-liquid equilibrium for water-air mixtures and the psychrometric chart. Students learn to determine humidity dew point and enthalpy of moist air streams.

title: Adsorption
description: Explains adsorption of gases and liquids onto solid surfaces. Students learn Langmuir and Freundlich isotherm models and their application in separation processes.

title: State Functions
description: Introduces state functions and path-independent thermodynamic properties. Students learn to distinguish state functions from path functions.

title: Steam Tables
description: Covers the use of steam tables to find thermodynamic properties of water. Students learn to read saturated and superheated steam tables for enthalpy entropy and specific volume.

title: Mechanical Energy Balance
description: Covers the mechanical energy balance including the Bernoulli equation with friction. Students learn to apply it to piping systems with pumps turbines and frictional losses.

title: Heat Capacities
description: Explains heat capacities for gases liquids and solids. Students learn to use heat capacity correlations to calculate enthalpy and internal energy changes.

title: Energy Balances with Phase Changes
description: Covers energy balances for processes involving phase changes. Students learn to account for latent heats of vaporization and fusion in enthalpy calculations.

title: Flash Separations
description: Explains flash drum calculations for vapor-liquid separation. Students learn to solve Rachford-Rice equations to find vapor fraction and equilibrium compositions.

title: Heats of Reaction
description: Covers standard heats of reaction and Hess's Law. Students learn to calculate reaction enthalpies using heats of formation and apply them to reactor energy balances.

title: Energy Balances with Reaction
description: Covers energy balances for reactors with chemical reactions. Students learn to account for heat of reaction alongside sensible heat changes in reactive systems.

title: Adiabatic Flame Temperature
description: Explains adiabatic flame temperature calculations for combustion. Students learn to find the maximum temperature reached when a fuel burns with no heat loss.

title: Introduction to First Law Closed Systems
description: Introduces the first law of thermodynamics for closed systems. Students learn to apply energy conservation to piston-cylinder and rigid-vessel problems.

title: Buoyancy
description: Covers buoyancy forces on submerged and floating objects. Students learn to apply Archimedes principle to determine buoyant force and object equilibrium in fluids.

title: Properties of Fluids
description: Explains key physical properties of fluids including density viscosity and surface tension. Students learn to identify and use these properties in fluid mechanics problems.

title: Hydrostatic Pressure
description: Covers pressure variation in static fluids. Students learn to apply the hydrostatic equation to calculate pressures at various depths in liquid systems.

title: Submerged Gates
description: Explains forces and moments on submerged flat gates and surfaces. Students learn to find the resultant hydrostatic force and its point of application.

title: Bernoullis Equation
description: Covers Bernoullis equation for frictionless flow. Students learn to apply energy conservation along a streamline to relate pressure velocity and elevation in fluid flow.

title: Viscosity and Shear Stress
description: Explains Newtons law of viscosity and shear stress in fluids. Students learn to relate shear stress to velocity gradients and distinguish Newtonian from non-Newtonian fluids.

title: Conservation of Mass
description: Covers the continuity equation for conservation of mass in fluid flow. Students learn to apply mass balance to steady and unsteady flow in pipes and open channels.

title: Introduction to Pipe Flow
description: Introduces laminar and turbulent pipe flow concepts. Students learn to calculate Reynolds number and identify flow regimes in circular pipes.

title: Calculating Velocity in Pipe Flow
description: Covers calculation of average and maximum velocities in pipe flow. Students learn to apply velocity profiles for laminar and turbulent flow conditions.

title: Characteristics of a Boundary Layer over a Flat Surface
description: Explains the development of a boundary layer over a flat plate. Students learn to characterize laminar and turbulent boundary layer thickness and drag forces.

title: Entrance Length in Pipe Flow
description: Covers hydrodynamic entrance length for flow developing in a pipe. Students learn to estimate the distance required to achieve fully developed laminar or turbulent flow.

title: Calculating Pressure Drop and Power in Pipe Flow
description: Explains calculation of frictional pressure drop and pump power in pipe flow. Students learn to use the Darcy-Weisbach equation and Moody chart for pipe system design.

title: Calculating Length and Equivalent Length in a Pipe
description: Covers calculation of pipe length using equivalent length method for fittings. Students learn to account for minor losses from valves and fittings in piping design.

title: Multipipe Systems
description: Explains analysis of pipe networks with multiple parallel and series branches. Students learn to apply flow distribution equations to solve multipipe system problems.

title: Linear Momentum
description: Covers the linear momentum equation for fluid systems. Students learn to apply Newtons second law to calculate forces exerted by fluids on pipes nozzles and vanes.

title: Derivation of a Pressure Field and Fluid at Rest
description: Covers the derivation of the hydrostatic pressure field from Navier-Stokes. Students learn how the momentum equation reduces to the pressure gradient equation for static fluids.

title: Using Boundary Conditions to Develop Velocity Profiles from the Navier-Stokes Equation
description: Explains how to apply boundary conditions to derive velocity profiles from the Navier-Stokes equation. Students solve for parabolic and other profiles in simple geometries.

title: Dimensional Analysis Pi Terms and Dimensionless Numbers
description: Covers Buckingham Pi theorem and dimensional analysis. Students learn to identify dimensionless groups governing fluid flow and heat and mass transfer problems.

title: Modeling and Similitude
description: Explains the use of scale models and similitude in fluid mechanics. Students learn geometric kinematic and dynamic similarity criteria for predicting full-scale behavior.

title: First Law - Closed Systems
description: Covers the first law of thermodynamics for closed systems. Students learn to calculate heat and work interactions for processes involving ideal gases and real substances.

title: First Law - Open Systems
description: Covers steady-state energy balances for open systems such as turbines and heat exchangers. Students learn to apply the first law to flow processes with shaft work.

title: Unsteady-State Energy Balances on Tanks
description: Covers energy balances for tanks with unsteady filling or draining. Students learn to apply the transient first law to open systems with time-varying inventories.

title: Entropy
description: Introduces entropy as a thermodynamic property. Students learn the second law entropy generation and entropy changes for reversible and irreversible processes.

title: Turbines and Compressors
description: Covers isentropic efficiency and performance of turbines and compressors. Students learn to calculate work and outlet conditions for adiabatic turbines and compressors.

title: Reversible and Irreversible Expansion and Compression Processes
description: Compares reversible and irreversible expansion and compression. Students learn to calculate work for isothermal adiabatic and polytropic processes.

title: Adiabatic Reversible Expansion and Compression
description: Covers isentropic expansion and compression processes. Students learn to calculate work and temperature changes for ideal gas and steam systems.

title: Carnot Cycle
description: Explains the Carnot cycle as the ideal heat engine cycle. Students learn to calculate Carnot efficiency and understand the maximum work obtainable from a heat source.

title: Rankine Cycle
description: Covers the Rankine cycle used in steam power plants. Students learn to analyze turbine pump boiler and condenser stages and calculate thermal efficiency.

title: Refrigeration Cycle
description: Explains the vapor-compression refrigeration cycle. Students learn to calculate COP heat removal and work input for refrigerators and heat pumps.

title: Throttling and Joule-Thomson Expansion
description: Covers throttling processes and the Joule-Thomson effect. Students learn to analyze pressure reduction through valves and the temperature change for real gases.

title: Fundamental Property Relations
description: Introduces Maxwell relations and fundamental thermodynamic property relationships. Students learn to derive thermodynamic identities and calculate property changes.

title: Liquefaction
description: Covers liquefaction of gases using the Linde and Claude processes. Students learn to analyze refrigeration cycles designed to produce liquid nitrogen oxygen or natural gas.

title: Thermodynamic Properties Phase Diagrams
description: Covers thermodynamic property diagrams including PV PT and TS diagrams. Students learn to read and interpret phase envelopes and property contours on these charts.

title: Departure Functions
description: Explains departure functions for calculating real fluid properties from ideal gas references. Students learn to compute enthalpy and entropy departures using equations of state.

title: Fugacity of a Single Component
description: Covers fugacity of pure components as a thermodynamic equilibrium criterion. Students learn to calculate fugacity from equations of state and use it in phase equilibrium.

title: Partial Molar Quantities
description: Explains partial molar properties in mixtures. Students learn to relate mixture properties to component partial molar quantities using the Gibbs-Duhem equation.

title: Fugacities of Mixtures
description: Covers fugacity of components in mixtures using fugacity coefficients. Students learn to apply equations of state to compute mixture fugacities for VLE calculations.

title: Chemical Potential
description: Explains chemical potential as the criterion for phase and reaction equilibrium. Students learn to use chemical potential to determine equilibrium conditions in mixtures.

title: Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium for Non-Ideal Solutions
description: Covers VLE for non-ideal liquid solutions using activity coefficient models. Students learn to apply Margules van Laar and Wilson equations for phase equilibrium.

title: Osmosis and Reverse Osmosis
description: Covers osmotic pressure and reverse osmosis membrane processes. Students learn to calculate osmotic pressure and design reverse osmosis systems for separation.

title: Absorption and Henrys Law
description: Explains absorption of gases into liquids using Henrys Law. Students learn to apply Henrys Law constants to determine gas solubility and design absorption columns.

title: Enthalpy of Mixing and Deviation from Raoults Law
description: Covers enthalpy of mixing and deviations from ideal Raoults Law behavior. Students learn to connect excess enthalpy with activity coefficients and non-ideal VLE.

title: Using a Cubic Equation of State to Determine VLE
description: Explains how to use cubic equations of state for VLE calculations. Students learn to solve for vapor and liquid phase fugacities and determine equilibrium compositions.

title: Gibbs Free Energy and Phase Separation
description: Covers Gibbs free energy of mixing and spinodal decomposition. Students learn to predict liquid-liquid phase separation from the shape of the Gibbs energy curve.

title: Partially-Miscible Liquids Phase Diagrams
description: Covers phase diagrams for partially miscible liquid pairs. Students learn to identify two-liquid-phase regions and determine equilibrium compositions using tie lines.

title: Immiscible Liquids Phase Diagrams
description: Covers phase diagrams for completely immiscible liquid pairs. Students learn to determine three-phase equilibrium temperature and analyze steam distillation processes.

title: Solid-Solid-Liquid Phase Diagrams
description: Explains phase diagrams for systems exhibiting solid-solid-liquid equilibria. Students learn to read eutectic diagrams and identify phase transitions with changing composition.

title: Azeotropes
description: Covers azeotrope formation in vapor-liquid equilibrium. Students learn to identify maximum and minimum boiling azeotropes and understand their impact on distillation.

title: Gas-Phase Chemical Equilibrium
description: Covers equilibrium constants and equilibrium composition for gas-phase reactions. Students learn to calculate Kp convert between bases and find equilibrium conversions.

title: Heterogeneous Chemical Equilibrium
description: Explains chemical equilibrium involving multiple phases. Students learn to derive equilibrium expressions and solve for equilibrium compositions.

title: Thermal Effects in Chemical Reactions
description: Covers the effect of temperature on equilibrium constants and reaction equilibrium. Students learn to apply van't Hoff equation and solve adiabatic reactor equilibrium problems.

title: Chemical Equilibrium for Multiple Reactions
description: Covers simultaneous chemical equilibria for systems with multiple reactions. Students learn to minimize Gibbs free energy or solve coupled equilibrium expressions.

title: Nonlinear Regression
description: Covers regression of rate law parameters from experimental data. Students learn to fit nonlinear kinetic models to concentration-time data using least squares methods.

title: Multiple Reactions and Selectivity
description: Explains parallel and series reaction networks and optimization of selectivity. Students learn to choose reactor type and operating conditions to maximize desired product yield.

title: Langmuir-Hinshelwood Kinetics
description: Covers Langmuir-Hinshelwood rate expressions for surface-catalyzed reactions. Students learn to derive and fit rate laws for adsorption reaction and desorption steps.

title: Diffusion and Reaction in Porous Catalysts
description: Covers internal diffusion limitations in porous catalyst pellets. Students learn to calculate Thiele modulus effectiveness factor and the impact of diffusion on observed reaction rates.

title: Isothermal Batch Reactors
description: Covers design equations for batch reactors with single reactions. Students learn to size isothermal batch reactors and determine reaction time for a given conversion.

title: Isothermal Continuous Stirred Tank Reactors
description: Covers design equations for isothermal continuous stirred tank reactors. Students learn to determine CSTR volume and conversion using steady-state mole balances.

title: Isothermal Plug Flow Reactors
description: Covers the design and performance analysis of isothermal plug flow reactors including PFR mole balances conversion profiles and sizing for various reaction orders.

title: Isothermal Semibatch Reactors
description: Introduces semibatch reactor operation under isothermal conditions examining time-dependent mole balances selectivity control and applications in chemical manufacturing.

title: Energy Balance in Steady-State PFR
description: Applies energy balances to steady-state plug flow reactors exploring the coupled ODEs for temperature and conversion profiles in exothermic and endothermic reactions.

title: Energy Balances in Stirred Tank Reactors
description: Covers energy balances for CSTRs including heat generation and removal curves steady-state temperature calculations and the impact of heat exchanger design on reactor performance.

title: Multiple Steady States in a Non-Isothermal CSTR
description: Investigates multiple steady states in non-isothermal CSTRs using heat generation and removal curves to identify stable and unstable operating points.

title: Pressure Drop in Packed Bed Reactors
description: Examines the Ergun equation and its application to pressure drop calculations in packed bed reactors including the effect of pressure on gas-phase reaction rates and conversion.

title: Steady-State Approximation and Rate-Determining Step
description: Explains the pseudo-steady-state hypothesis and rate-limiting step concept used in deriving rate expressions for complex reaction mechanisms in chemical kinetics.

title: Enzyme Kinetics
description: Explores enzymatic reaction kinetics using the Michaelis-Menten model covering substrate concentration effects maximum reaction rates and inhibition mechanisms in biochemical systems.

title: Polymerization Kinetics
description: Introduces the kinetics of polymerization reactions including chain-growth and step-growth mechanisms molecular weight distributions and rate expressions for polymer synthesis.

title: Solving Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Covers numerical and analytical methods for solving ODEs encountered in reactor design including initial value problems and the use of software tools for reaction engineering applications.

title: Residence Time Distribution
description: Covers the theory and application of residence time distribution analysis for characterizing non-ideal flow patterns in reactors including step and pulse tracer experiments.

title: Polymerization Reactors
description: Explores reactor design for polymerization processes covering conversion molecular weight control and the design of batch CSTR and tubular reactors for polymer production.

title: Single-Stage Batch Distillation
description: Covers the fundamentals of single-stage batch distillation including Rayleigh equation differential distillation and the effect of relative volatility on separation efficiency.

title: Multistage Batch Distillation
description: Extends batch distillation concepts to multistage columns exploring the role of reflux ratio number of stages and column efficiency in achieving desired product purity.

title: McCabe-Thiele Diagrams
description: Introduces the McCabe-Thiele graphical method for binary distillation column design covering operating lines q-lines equilibrium stages and the minimum reflux ratio concept.

title: Absorption Columns
description: Covers the design and analysis of absorption columns for removing gaseous components including number of transfer units height of a transfer unit and operating line construction.

title: Stripping Columns
description: Examines stripping column design for removing dissolved gases from liquids covering equilibrium stages operating lines and the use of stripping factor to optimize column performance.

title: Hunter-Nash Method for Liquid-Liquid Extraction
description: Applies the Hunter-Nash graphical method to liquid-liquid extraction design covering extraction stages solvent selection and the determination of raffinate and extract compositions.

title: Single-Effect Evaporators
description: Covers the design and analysis of single-effect evaporators including energy and mass balances boiling point elevation and steam economy for concentrating liquid solutions.

title: Multi-Effect Evaporators
description: Extends evaporation concepts to multi-effect systems analyzing the trade-offs between steam economy and capital cost for concentrating solutions in food and chemical industries.

title: Lumped Capacitance Method for Analyzing Transient Conduction Problems
description: Covers lumped capacitance analysis for transient heat conduction including the Biot number criterion exponential temperature decay and applications in quenching and cooling.

title: Transient Conduction in a Sphere with Spatial Effects
description: Extends transient conduction analysis to spherical geometries with significant internal temperature gradients using one-term approximation and Heisler charts for temperature distribution.

title: Transient Conduction into a Semi-Infinite Solid
description: Covers transient heat conduction in semi-infinite solids subjected to sudden surface temperature changes including error function solutions and penetration depth estimation.

title: Convective Heat Transfer over a Flat Plate
description: Examines external forced convection heat transfer over a flat plate covering boundary layer development local and average Nusselt number correlations and laminar-to-turbulent transition.

title: Free Convection
description: Covers natural convection heat transfer driven by buoyancy forces including the Grashof and Rayleigh numbers vertical plate correlations and applications in electronic cooling and building insulation.
